arxiv-2012-08521.title: A Swift Fix for Nuclear Outbursts Journal: AJ Facilities: Swift (UVOT) ( Roming et al. 2005 ) linmix ( Kelly 2007 )
arxiv-2012-08521.creator: Jason T. Hinkle, Thomas W.-S. Holoien, Benjamin. J. Shappee, Katie Auchettl
arxiv-2012-08521.description: Abstract In November 2020, the Swift team announced an update to the UltraViolet and Optical Telescope calibration to correct for the loss of sensitivity over time. This correction affects observations in the three near ultraviolet (UV) filters, by up to 0.3 mag in some cases.

arxiv-2104-07933.title: Second cohomology groups of the Hopf ∗ -algebras associated to universal unitary quantum groups
arxiv-2104-07933.creator: Biswarup Das, Uwe Franz, Anna Kula, Adam Skalski
arxiv-2104-07933.description: Abstract . We compute the second (and the first) cohomology groups of ∗ -algebras associated to the universal quantum unitary groups of not necesarily Kac type, extending our earlier results for the free unitary group U d + U_{d}^{+} . The extended setup forces us to use infinite-dimensional representations to construct the cocycles.

arxiv-2110-05095.title: 𝚇𝚘𝚘𝚔𝚂𝚞𝚞𝚝 \mathtt{XookSuut} : a bayesian tool for modeling circular and non–circular flows on 2D velocity maps
arxiv-2110-05095.creator: C. López-Cobá, Lihwai Lin, Sebastián F. Sánchez
arxiv-2110-05095.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by C. López-Cobá, Lihwai Lin, Sebastián F. Sánchez. En este artículo presentamos 𝚇𝚘𝚘𝚔𝚂𝚞𝚞𝚝 \mathtt{XookSuut} , una implenetación en Python del algoritmo 𝙳𝚒𝚜𝚔𝙵𝚒𝚝 \mathtt{DiskFit} , optimizado para realizar inferencia Bayesiana de manera robusta sobre parámetros que describen modelos cinemáticos de rotación circular y no circular an galaxias.

arxiv-2202-00717.title: Pipeflow: An Efficient Task-Parallel Pipeline Programming Framework using Modern C++ Conference: ACM Symposium on High-Performance Parallel and Distributed Computing; June 27–July 1, 2022; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA
arxiv-2202-00717.creator: Cheng-Hsiang Chiu, Tsung-Wei Huang, Zizheng Guo, Yibo Lin
arxiv-2202-00717.description: Abstract . Pipeline is a fundamental parallel programming pattern. Mainstream pipeline programming frameworks count on data abstractions to perform pipeline scheduling. This design is convenient for data-centric pipeline applications but inefficient for algorithms that only exploit task parallelism in pipeline. As a result, we introduce a new task-parallel pipeline programming framework called Pipeflow .

arxiv-2204-10141.title: Red Dragon: A Redshift-Evolving Gaussian Mixture Model for Galaxies 2020 Red Dragon: A Redshift-Evolving Gaussian Mixture Model for Galaxies – G.1
arxiv-2204-10141.creator: William K. Black, August Evrard
arxiv-2204-10141.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by William K. Black, August Evrard. Precision-era optical cluster cosmology calls for a precise definition of the red sequence (RS), consistent across redshift. To this end, we present the Red Dragon algorithm: an error-corrected multivariate Gaussian mixture model (GMM). Simultaneous use of multiple colors and smooth evolution of GMM parameters result in a continuous RS and blue cloud (BC) characterization across redshift, avoiding the discontinuities of red fraction inherent in swapping RS selection colors.

arxiv-2206-06849.title: On the Gauss-Manin Connection and Real Singularities
arxiv-2206-06849.creator: Lars Andersen
arxiv-2206-06849.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Lars Andersen. We prove that to each real singularity f : ( ℝ n + 1 , 0 ) → ( ℝ , 0 ) f:(\mathbb{R}^{n+1},0)\to(\mathbb{R},0) one can associate two systems of differential equations 𝔤 f k ± \mathfrak{g}^{k\pm}_{f} which are pushforwards in the category of 𝒟 \mathcal{D} -modules over ℝ ± \mathbb{R}^{\pm} , of the sheaf of real analytic functions on the total space of the positive, respectively negative, Milnor fibration.

arxiv-2301-00654.title: On the existence and uniqueness of solution to a stochastic chemotaxis-Navier-stokes model
arxiv-2301-00654.creator: E. Hausenblas ∗ , B. Jidjou Moghomye ∗ and P. A. Razafimandimby ∗∗
arxiv-2301-00654.description: Abstract . In this article, we study a mathematical system which models the dynamic of the collective behaviour of oxygen-driven swimming bacteria in an aquatic fluid flowing in a two dimensional bounded domain under stochastic perturbation. This model can be seen as a stochastic version of Chemotaxis-Navier-Stokes model. We prove the existence of a unique (probabilistic) strong solution.

arxiv-2305-06919.title: Reliability Improvement of Circular k k -out-of- n n : G Balanced Systems through Center of Gravity
arxiv-2305-06919.creator: Yongkyu Cho, Seung Min Baik, Young Myoung Ko
arxiv-2305-06919.description: Abstract This paper considers a circular k k -out-of- n n : G balanced system equipped with homogeneous and stationary units. Building on previous research by Endharta et al. [ 5 ] , we propose a new balance definition in circular k k -out-of- n n : G balanced systems based on the concept of center of gravity.

arxiv-2311-00873.title: Low-latency Real-time Voice Conversion on CPU
arxiv-2311-00873.creator: Konstantine Sadov, Matthew Hutter, Asara Near
arxiv-2311-00873.description: Abstract We adapt the architectures of previous audio manipulation and generation neural networks to the task of real-time any-to-one voice conversion. Our resulting model, LLVC ( L ow-latency L ow-resource V oice C onversion), has a latency of under 20ms at a bitrate of 16kHz and runs nearly 2.8x faster than real-time on a consumer CPU.

arxiv-2410-13008.title: When all directed cycles have length three
arxiv-2410-13008.creator: Paul Seymour
arxiv-2410-13008.description: Abstract We give a construction to build all digraphs with the property that every directed cycle has length three. 1 Introduction A digraph (in this paper) means a directed graph without loops or parallel edges (but we permit directed cyles of length two). A digraph is \ell -cyclic if all its directed cycles have length \ell .

arxiv-2411-16882.title: Polarization and dynamic phases of aligning active matter in periodic obstacle arrays
arxiv-2411-16882.creator: Daniel Canavello 1 , C. Reichhardt 2 , C.J.O Reichhardt 2 , and Clécio C. de Souza Silva 1
arxiv-2411-16882.description: Abstract We numerically examine a system of monodisperse self-propelled particles interacting with each other via simple steric forces and aligning torques moving through a periodic array of obstacles. Without obstacles, this system shows a transition to a polarized or aligned state for critical alignment parameters.

arxiv-2412-01441.title: LMAct: A Benchmark for In-Context Imitation Learning with Long Multimodal Demonstrations
arxiv-2412-01441.creator: Anian Ruoss, Fabio Pardo, Harris Chan, Bonnie Li, Volodymyr Mnih, Tim Genewein
arxiv-2412-01441.description: Abstract In this paper, we present a benchmark to pressure-test today’s frontier models’ multimodal decision-making capabilities in the very long-context regime (up to one million tokens) and investigate whether these models can learn from large numbers of expert demonstrations in their context. We evaluate the performance of Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Flash, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Gemini 2.

arxiv-2501-03846.title: Isogeny graphs with level structures arising from the Verschiebung map
arxiv-2501-03846.creator: Antonio Lei, Katharina Müller
arxiv-2501-03846.description: Abstract . We enhance an isogeny graph of elliptic curves by incorporating level structures defined by bases of the kernels of iterates of the Verschiebung map. We extend several previous results on isogeny graphs with level structures defined by geometric points to these graphs.

arxiv-2503-13034.title: TA-GNN: Physics Inspired Time-Agnostic Graph Neural Network for Finger Motion Prediction
arxiv-2503-13034.creator: Tinghui Li, Pamuditha Somarathne, Zhanna Sarsenbayeva, Anusha Withana
arxiv-2503-13034.description: Abstract . Continuous prediction of finger joint movement using historical joint positions/rotations is vital in a multitude of applications, especially related to virtual reality, computer graphics, robotics, and rehabilitation. However, finger motions are highly articulated with multiple degrees of freedom, making them significantly harder to model and predict.

arxiv-2503-14707.title: Bribery for Coalitions in Parliamentary Elections
arxiv-2503-14707.creator: Hodaya Barr, Yonatan Aumann, Sarit Kraus
arxiv-2503-14707.description: Abstract We study the computational complexity of bribery in parliamentary voting, in settings where the briber is (also) interested in the success of an entire set of political parties - a “coalition” - rather than an individual party. We introduce two variants of the problem: the Coalition-Bribery Problem (CB) and the Coalition-Bribery-with-Preferred-party Problem (CBP).

arxiv-2504-15923.title: Bayesian sample size calculations for external validation studies of risk prediction models
arxiv-2504-15923.creator: Mohsen Sadatsafavi, Paul Gustafson, Solmaz Setayeshgar, Laure Wynants, Richard D. Riley
arxiv-2504-15923.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mohsen Sadatsafavi, Paul Gustafson, Solmaz Setayeshgar, Laure Wynants, Richard D. Riley. Contemporary sample size calculations for external validation of risk prediction models require users to specify fixed values of assumed model performance metrics alongside target precision levels (e.g., 95% CI widths). However, due to the finite samples of previous studies, our knowledge of true model performance in the target population is uncertain, and so choosing fixed values represents an incomplete picture.

arxiv-2507-16976.title: A resource theoretical unification of Mpemba effects: classical and quantum
arxiv-2507-16976.creator: Alessandro Summer, Mattia Moroder, Laetitia P. Bettmann, Xhek Turkeshi, Iman Marvian, John Goold
arxiv-2507-16976.description: Abstract The Mpemba effect originally referred to the observation that, under certain thermalizing dynamics, initially hotter samples can cool faster than colder ones. This effect has since been generalized to other anomalous relaxation behaviors even beyond classical domains, such as symmetry restoration in quantum systems.

arxiv-2508-20750.title: Specializing General-purpose LLM Embeddings for Implicit Hate Speech Detection across Datasets Conference: Proceedings of the 2nd International Workshop on Diffusion of Harmful Content on Online Web; October 27–28, 2025; Dublin, Ireland Proceedings of the 2nd International Workshop on Diffusion of H
arxiv-2508-20750.creator: Vassiliy Cheremetiev, Quang Long Ho Ngo, Chau Ying Kot, Alina Elena Baia, Andrea Cavallaro
arxiv-2508-20750.description: Abstract . Implicit hate speech (IHS) is indirect language that conveys prejudice or hatred through subtle cues, sarcasm or coded terminology. IHS is challenging to detect as it does not include explicit derogatory or inflammatory words. To address this challenge, task-specific pipelines can be complemented with external knowledge or additional information such as context, emotions and sentiment data.

arxiv-2509-04322.title: Characteristic Energy Behavior Profiling of Non-Residential Buildings
arxiv-2509-04322.creator: 1 st Haley Dozier, 2 nd Althea Henslee
arxiv-2509-04322.description: Abstract Due to the threat of changing climate and extreme weather events, the infrastructure of the United States Army installations is at risk. More than ever, climate resilience measures are needed to protect facility assets that support critical missions and help generate readiness.

arxiv-2512-23822.title: Resonant Magneto-phonon Emission by Supersonic Electrons in Ultra-high Mobility Two-dimensional System
arxiv-2512-23822.creator: Z. T. Wang, M. Hilke, N. Fong, D. G. Austing, S. A. Studenikin, K. W. West, L. N. Pfeiffer
arxiv-2512-23822.description: Abstract We investigate resonant acoustic phonon scattering in the magneto-resistivity of an ultra-high mobility two-dimensional electron gas system subject to DC current in the temperature range 10 mK to 3.9 K. For a DC current density of ∼ \sim 1.

arxiv-2601-11622.title: Dynamical Systems Analysis Reveals Functional Regimes in Large Language Models
arxiv-2601-11622.creator: Hassan Ugail, Newton Howard
arxiv-2601-11622.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Hassan Ugail, Newton Howard. Large language models perform text generation through high-dimensional internal dynamics, yet the temporal organisation of these dynamics remains poorly understood. Most interpretability approaches emphasise static representations or causal interventions, leaving temporal structure largely unexplored. Drawing on neuroscience, where temporal integration and metastability are core markers of neural organisation, we adapt these concepts to transformer models and discuss a composite dynamical metric, computed from activation time-series during autoregressive generation.

arxiv-2604-04113.title: Heavy and heavy-light tensor and axial-tensor mesons in the Covariant Spectator Theory Thanks: Presented at Excited QCD Workshop 2026, Granada, Spain
arxiv-2604-04113.creator: Elmar P. Biernat Alfred Stadler

arxiv-2606-14730.creator: Parthsarthi Rawat

pmc-10725692.title: Integrated Network Pharmacology and Experimental Approach to Investigate the Protective Effect of Jin Gu Lian Capsule on Rheumatoid Arthritis by Inhibiting Inflammation via IL-17/NF-κB Pathway
pmc-10725692.creator: Tengfei Chen, Sihan Li, Dongyin Lian, Qin Hu, Hongping Hou, Delian Niu, Han Li, Ling Song, Yunhang Gao, Ying Chen, Xiaoru Hu, Jianrong Li, Zuguang Ye, Bo Peng, Guangping Zhang
pmc-10725692.description: PurposeThis study aimed to investigate the main pharmacological action and underlying mechanisms of Jin Gu Lian Capsule (JGL) against rheumatoid arthritis (RA) based on network pharmacology and experimental verification.MethodsNetwork pharmacology approaches were performed to explore the core active compounds of JGL, key therapeutic targets, and signaling pathways. Molecular docking was used to predict the binding affinity of compounds with targets.

pmc-11415624.title: ﻿Two new species of Dendrostoma (Erythrogloeaceae, Diaporthales) associated with Castaneamollissima canker disease in China
pmc-11415624.creator: Ning Jiang, Xiaojie Qi, Baoxin Qi, Fang Cai, Han Xue, Yong Li
pmc-11415624.description: ﻿AbstractThe genus Dendrostoma is known to inhabit tree barks associated with branch canker diseases in China and several countries of Europe. Previous studies indicated that species of Dendrostoma prefer inhabiting fagaceous hosts, especially species of Castanea. In the present study, we obtained four isolates from cankered branches of Chinese chestnut (C.mollissima) in Rizhao City, Shandong Province, China.

pmc-11513540.title: Radiometric hazard assessment of soil and water samples adjacent to Bangladesh's first nuclear power plant before commissioning: Insights into human health and environmental radiological dynamics
pmc-11513540.creator: S. Yeasmin, S.K. Das, M.M. Mahfuz Siraz, A.F.M. Mizanur Rahman, M.S. Rahman
pmc-11513540.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The current study provides a comprehensive examination of both natural and anthropogenic activity concentrations found in soil and surface water samples near the Rooppur nuclear power plant (RNPP), the first of its kind under construction in Bangladesh. The investigation covers a range of activity concentrations including 226Ra, 232Th, and 40K in fifty soil and fifty water samples, revealing values ranging from 18 to 38, 18–51, and 310–560 Bqkg−1 for soil, and 2.1–6.1, 2.1–5.5, and 67–115 Bqkg−1 for water, respectively.

pmc-11600549.title: Influenza neuraminidase mutations and resistance to neuraminidase inhibitors
pmc-11600549.creator: Jiapeng Xu, Qiting Luo, Yuanyuan Huang, Jieyu Li, Wei Ye, Ran Yan, Xinrui Zhou, Zhendan He, Ge Liu, Qinchang Zhu
pmc-11600549.description: Mutations in influenza virus neuraminidase (NA) can lead to viral resistance to NA inhibitors (NAIs). To update global influenza NA mutations and resistance to NAIs, we investigated epidemic information from global regions for NAIs-resistant influenza strains and analyzed their NA mutations. Drug-resistant mutations in NA, especially new mutations occurred in 2016-2024, were updated.

pmc-11607962.title: Analysis of the impact of China Healthcare Security diagnosis-related groups payment reform on the hospitalization costs for uvulopalatopharyngoplasty in obstructive sleep apnea patients at Hospital C
pmc-11607962.creator: Mengying Li, Jing Yang, Jiyong Shen, Jinkun Xu, Debin Gu
pmc-11607962.description: BackgroundAs part of China’s medical insurance-related grouping payment reform, public hospitals, which are the primary providers of medical insurance services, face remarkable pressure to control costs. This study examined uvulopalatopharyngoplasty (UPPP) surgery for patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) at Hospital C to identify factors influencing inpatient costs and assess the impact of payment reform on treatment practices.

pmc-11658148.title: Medical chart-reported alcohol consumption, substance use, and mental health issues in association with HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) nonadherence among gay, bisexual, and other men-who-have-sex-with-men
pmc-11658148.creator: Paul A Shuper, Narges Joharchi, Thepikaa Varatharajan, Isaac I Bogoch, Mona Loutfy, Philippe El-Helou, Kevin Giolma, Kevin Woodward, Jürgen Rehm
pmc-11658148.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundAlthough some evidence suggests that alcohol, substance use, and mental health issues diminish adherence to HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) among gay, bisexual, and other men-who-have-sex-with-men (gbMSM), findings are somewhat inconsistent and have primarily derived from studies involving non-random samples. Medical chart extraction can provide unique insight by in part surmounting sampling-related limitations, as data for entire PrEP clinic populations can be examined.

pmc-12477937.title: Predictors of immediate survival in Emergency Department cardiac arrest in Ethiopia: Insights from a resource-limited setting
pmc-12477937.creator: Zigale Tilaye Ayalew, Alemayehu Beharu Tekle, Molla Asnake Kebede, Melaku T Berhanu, Ashenafi Jemal, Etsegent akloge
pmc-12477937.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIn-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) in Emergency Departments (EDs) remains a leading cause of mortality, particularly in low-resource countries. This study aims to identify the clinical characteristics and predictors of immediate survival among ED cardiac arrest patients in Ethiopian hospitals.MethodsA retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted among 215 adult patients who experienced IHCA in the EDs of Saint Paul’s Hospital Millennium Medical College and Addis Ababa Burn, Emergency, and Trauma Hospital between January 2022 and December 2023.

pmc-13021485.title: Ruxolitinib reverses systemic vasculitis driven by JAK2 V617F–mutated essential thrombocythemia: a case report
pmc-13021485.creator: Yutaro Ashida, Shinji Ota, Nao Ishidoya, Yasuhisa Murai, Kyoko Amenomori, Keisuke Hasui, Shogo Kawaguchi, Satoko Yamaguchi, Hiroto Hiraga, Kosuke Kamata, Hiroaki Ichikawa, Hirofumi Tomita, Zaiqiang Yu, Masahito Minakawa, Hirotake Sakuraba
pmc-13021485.description: BackgroundVasculitis associated with myeloproliferative neoplasms is rare, and reports on its treatment are limited. Herein, we report a case of Janus Kinase2 (JAK2) V617F mutation–positive essential thrombocythemia (ET) associated with vasculitis.Case presentationA 60-year-old man with JAK2 V617F mutation–positive ET underwent coronary artery bypass grafting after recurrent myocardial infarctions and coronary stent occlusions.

pmc-13224383.title: Decoding the causal drivers of spatial cellular topology
pmc-13224383.creator: Prannav Shankar, Huan Liang, Uthsav Chitra, Rohit Singh
pmc-13224383.description: SummaryDecoding how cells influence and communicate with each other in space is fundamental for understanding tissue organization. However, existing approaches either overlook spatial context entirely or rely solely on local cell-cell adjacency, failing to capture how global tissue topology shapes cellular communication.

pmc-13287407.title: Pseudo-slimy: A novel phenomenon to evoke stickiness perception
pmc-13287407.creator: Takahiro Kawabe, Tao Morisaki, Yusuke Ujitoko
pmc-13287407.description: Everyday materials such as honey, shampoo, and oil are often described not only in terms of their viscosity but also by the sense of stickiness they evoke during contact and separation. Although previous studies have identified visual cues that support the perception of viscosity, the visual basis of stickiness perception, particularly in interactive contexts, remains poorly understood.

pmc-13306472.title: Real-Time Stress Experiences and Physiological and Psychological Responses Among LGBTQ+ Young Adults: Findings from the Stress and Heart Pilot Study
pmc-13306472.creator: Hee-Jin Jun, Kang-Hyuk Lee, Dulce Urueta Tapia, Jerel P. Calzo, Heather L. Corliss

pmc-13316266.title: Contrastive multi-view representation learning for multi-camera plant phenotyping: A cotton field study
pmc-13316266.creator: Daniel Petti, Changying Li, Ninghao Liu
pmc-13316266.description: Attempts to deploy computer vision in agricultural tasks often suffer from a shortage of annotated data. One strategy to alleviate the impact of limited data is Self-Supervised Learning (SSL), which involves pre-training a model on a pretext task that utilizes automatically generated annotations.

pmc-13575151.title: Solution-phase transition zones govern crystallographic perfection in metal halide perovskite single crystals
pmc-13575151.creator: Zhongyi Lin, Lei Li, Tanhao Zhang, Hengyu Zhang, Fuyi Zhou, Lixiang Wang, Jingyi Sun, Yanjun Fang, Pok Fung Chan, Hengkai Zhang, Xinhui Lu, Deren Yang, Zhenyi Ni
pmc-13575151.description: Despite rapid progress in solution-grown metal halide perovskite single crystals for optoelectronic applications, further enhancement of their intrinsic crystallographic quality through solution engineering remains challenging. In particular, the fundamental links between precursor solution properties and crystal quality, as well as a universal mechanism governing crystallization from solution, remains poorly understood.

pmc-9617234.title: The updated Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research based on user feedback
pmc-9617234.creator: Laura J. Damschroder, Caitlin M. Reardon, Marilla A. Opra Widerquist et al.
pmc-9617234.description: Peer-reviewed research article (PubMed Central). Many implementation efforts fail, even with highly developed plans for execution, because contextual factors can be powerful forces working against implementation in the real world.
